description: Hi everyone, I’m Amos Seleem Oluwarantimi, a Cell Biology and Genetics student with a growing interest in AI, data science, environmental science, and technology. I’m looking to connect with people who are passionate about technology, science, and problem-solving. Skills in Python, data analysis, GIS, remote sensing, AI/machine learning, web or app development, and UI/UX would be especially useful.
summary: Farmers around the world navigate shifting temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, water shortages, extreme weather, and declining soil health. These pressures make it difficult to choose crop rotations that protect fields, conserve water, and support long‑term resilience. Your challenge is to create a decision‑support tool that uses NASA Earth observations along with local soil information, crop characteristics, and farmer priorities to help farmers explore rotation strategies that could strengthen soil health and adapt their farms to changing conditions.
details: Team Alpha Crop Advisor helps Nigerian farmers decide what to plant and when. The farmer picks their farm on a map and optionally lists their last three crops. The system then combines three models. A rainfall estimator forecasts monthly rain from NASA POWER climate history. A soil quality model reads soil pH, texture and nitrogen from ISRIC SoilGrids and estimates what previous crops removed from or added to the soil's nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium. A crop advisor scores each crop against the rain and soil, then returns the top 5 crops with the best planting and harvest months. Benefits and impact: It gives smallholder farmers location-specific planning guidance without a lab test or expensive consultation. It reduces the risk of planting at the wrong time, and it shows when a crop is draining soil nutrients, which supports more sustainable farming and better yields. Tools: Python (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, requests) for the models. NASA POWER, ISRIC SoilGrids and OpenStreetMap supply the data. A JavaScript/HTML demo with a Leaflet map is the interface. Creativity: It joins climate, soil and crop science in one tool. The crop nutrient figures come from peer-reviewed research. Built-in safety checks never invent data, fall back to a plain historical average when the machine-learning model isn't better, and label every result with a confidence score.
